[One who has a garden atop the olive press of his fellow, containing one section]: An olive press where they make oil that is built into the thickness of a mountain, with a garden on top of it, and the ceiling of the olive press—which is the arch—was breached by four tefachim or more, behold, the owner of the garden descends and sows his garden below. He shall sow things that do not require rain until the owner of the press makes arches for his olive press and the upper one repairs the soil of his garden. This means that he provides the soil [Rashi] and sows his garden, as in siman 164, section 1, where the upper one provides the plaster and the lower one the ceiling; so too here, the lower one makes the arch and the upper one the soil. And even according to the "there are those who say" there, that the upper one provides everything, that is because the homeowner does not need the ceiling of the house since he has the ceiling of the upper story, but here, where the owner of the press needs the arch just as the owner of the garden does, they agree that the law is so, as I have written. And even with partners the law is so [Tur]. And as long as he does not make the arch, he may sow everything below, and we do not say that he should sow everything above and in the place of the breach sow below, for he is not obligated to exert himself and sow in two places [Gemara Bava Metzia].
